text: The original attention mechanism divides the query‑key dot products by a constant (specifically \(1/\sqrt{d_k}\)) before applying softmax to prevent the dot products from becoming too large as the dimensionality \(d_k\) grows, which would push the softmax into regions with extremely small gradients. This scaling keeps the values in a range where the softmax is more stable and trainable. [C:attention:9]

The papers don’t say that learned positional embeddings worked better than the sinusoidal version. They report that the two approaches produced nearly identical results, so no clear advantage was found for the learned embeddings.
The big Transformer model has approximately 2.3 × 10⁹ parameters. [C:attention:22]
Moshi’s Depth Transformer uses 6 layers and a model dimension of 1024. [C:moshi:41]

The smoothing module in H‑Net converts the discrete chunk boundaries produced by the routing module into smooth, interpolated representations. By attenuating the effect of uncertain or noisy boundaries, it improves the learnability of the model and allows the downstream network to process a more stable, continuous signal. [C:dynchunk:9]

The hierarchical network consists of three stages: (i) a small encoder that processes raw data, (ii) a main network that operates on the down‑sampled, compressed chunks, and (iii) a decoder that upsamples the compressed representations back to the original resolution. [C:dynchunk:6]

Moshi’s Inner Monologue is a training and inference procedure that jointly models text and audio tokens. By first predicting time‑aligned text tokens as a prefix to audio tokens, the model can fully exploit the knowledge from the text modality while remaining a speech‑to‑speech system, which improves linguistic quality and enables streaming speech recognition and text‑to‑speech.
